policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV prints 'the Son of God' in the text and relegates the omission to a note ('Some ancient authorities omit the Son of God'), so the base short reading is excluded; r01 and r02 differ only by the article before theou, which English cannot show.
ASV 'Even as it is written' renders Kathos and Hos alike; the verse's textual note concerns 'in the prophets', not the conjunction.
ASV text reads 'in Isaiah the prophet' and its textual note explicitly relegates the rival: 'Some ancient authorities read in the prophets.'
'Behold, I send my messenger' supplies the subject pronoun from the first-person verb; an added ego is not separately visible in English.
ASV ends the citation 'Who shall prepare thy way' with nothing answering the added emprosthen sou ('before thee').

ASV renders the participle as a relative clause, 'John came, who baptized in the wilderness', the rendering an articular ho baptizon calls for; the anarthrous reading would give 'John came baptizing'.
ASV coordinates the two participles, 'who baptized in the wilderness and preached', which requires the kai the base text lacks.

ASV attaches 'all' to the Jerusalemites ('and all they of Jerusalem; and they were baptized'), not to the baptizing, so RP's kai ebaptizonto pantes ('were all baptized') is excluded; the remaining two readings differ only in punctuation.
English orders agent and place phrases idiomatically ('baptized of him in the river Jordan'); either Greek order yields the same clause.
ASV's opening 'And John was clothed' is what ASV writes for kai and often for de alike; nothing else distinguishes the readings.
ASV leaves men untranslated as usual ('I baptized you in water; but he shall baptize you'), so its presence or absence is invisible.
ASV writes 'in water' with the marginal 'Or, with'; a bare dative hudati and en hudati are both rendered so.
'in the Holy Spirit' (margin 'Or, with') renders the instrumental dative with or without en.
'was baptized of John in the Jordan' places agent and place by English idiom; the Greek order of the two phrases is not recoverable.
euthus and eutheos are the same word in two forms; ASV renders either 'straightway'.
ASV 'coming up out of the water' renders ek; apo would give 'from the water', which ASV consistently distinguishes.
'as a dove' renders hos and hosei indifferently.
'descending upon him' is the only natural English for either eis auton or ep' auton after a verb of descent, and ASV attaches no 'Greek into' gloss here.
ASV keeps the second person throughout the voice's words: 'Thou art my beloved Son, in thee I am well pleased' renders en soi, not the relative en ho ('in whom').
ASV has 'And he was in the wilderness forty days' with no 'there'; the added ekei would be rendered.
'forty days' fixes English order regardless of the Greek order, and the two spellings of the numeral are identical in sense.
ASV opens the verse 'Now after John was delivered up', and the adversative 'Now' answers Meta de, not the connective Kai meta.
ASV reads 'preaching the gospel of God' with nothing for the added tes basileias ('of the kingdom').
'And passing along by the sea of Galilee' renders Kai paragon; RP's Peripaton de would give 'And as he walked'.
ASV has 'Andrew the brother of Simon' with no possessive; the added autou would give 'his brother'.
'casting a net in the sea' is ASV's rendering of the single verb amphiballontas as much as of ballontas amphiblestron; the object is idiomatic either way.
'straightway' renders euthus and eutheos alike.
ASV reads 'they left the nets', not 'their nets', so the added auton is absent.
'And going on a little further' renders probas with no 'from thence' answering ekeithen.
'And straightway he called them' renders either form of the adverb.
'straightway on the sabbath day' renders euthus and eutheos alike.
ASV has two verbs, 'he entered into the synagogue and taught', which requires the participle eiselthon; the base reading has only edidasken eis ten synagogen.
ASV opens 'And straightway there was in their synagogue a man', so the adverb the rival omits is rendered.
The demoniac's speech begins 'What have we to do with thee'; nothing renders the prefixed interjection Ea.
'crying with a loud voice' fits phonesan phone megale and kraxan phone megale equally.
'they were all amazed' renders hapantes and pantes without distinction.
ASV reads 'they questioned among themselves', the reflexive pros heautous; WH's autous makes the pronoun the subject of the infinitive and leaves no 'among themselves'.

ASV has one question and an exclamation, 'What is this? a new teaching!', matching the short base; RP's Tis he didache he kaine haute hoti would give a second question, 'What new doctrine is this? for...'.
ASV's opening 'And the report of him went out' is written for kai and for a sentence-initial de alike.
'went out straightway everywhere' renders pantachou, which the rival omits.
'And straightway' renders euthus and eutheos alike.
ASV text is plural, 'when they were come out ... they came into the house', and its note relegates the singular: 'Some ancient authorities read when he was come out of the synagogue, he came etc.'
'and straightway they tell him of her' renders either form of the adverb.
'took her by the hand' is English idiom for kratesas tes cheiros with or without autes; the pronoun ASV prints already serves 'raised her up'.
'and the fever left her' has no 'immediately' answering the added eutheos.
'when the sun did set' renders both aorist forms edu and edusen identically.
'And all the city was gathered together at the door' fixes English order; the Greek order of the copula and subject is not recoverable from it.
ASV text ends 'because they knew him' and its note relegates the addition: 'Many ancient authorities add to be Christ.'
'Simon and they that were with him followed after him' is the same English whether the Greek verb is singular agreeing with the first subject or plural.
The article on a proper name is not rendered; 'Simon' answers Simon and ho Simon alike.

ASV coordinates two finite verbs, 'and they found him, and say unto him', answering heuron auton kai; ASV keeps participles as participles, so RP's heurontes would give 'and having found him, they say'.
'All are seeking thee' fixes verb before object in English whatever the Greek order.
ASV reads 'Let us go elsewhere into the next towns', rendering allachou, which the rival omits.
'for to this end came I forth' is the aorist exelthon; ASV renders the perfect exelelutha as 'am I come forth'.
'And he went into their synagogues ... preaching' has a verb of motion, elthen; RP's en with the participle would give 'he was preaching in their synagogues'.
ASV reads 'into their synagogues', the accusative eis tas synagogas; en tais synagogais would be 'in their synagogues'.
ASV has both the object and the connective: 'kneeling down to him, and saying unto him' requires auton kai; the base has neither and r01 lacks the object.
ASV names no subject at the verse opening ('And being moved with compassion, he stretched forth his hand'); RP's Ho de Iesous would give 'And Jesus'.
'And being moved with compassion' renders splanchnistheis; orgistheis would be 'being moved with anger'.
'and touched him' fixes verb before object in English whatever the Greek order.
ASV reads 'And straightway the leprosy departed from him' with nothing for RP's eipontos autou ('when he had spoken').
'and straightway sent him out' renders euthus and eutheos alike.
'was without in desert places' renders the locative ep' eremois topois and en eremois topois alike.
'from every quarter' renders pantothen and pantachothen without distinction.
